facts.text: Bloomfield Hills is a small city in Oakland County on the Woodward Corridor, and it is surrounded on most sides by Bloomfield Township, a separate municipality.
The city sits about 20 miles northwest of Detroit and is primarily residential, known for grand estates, tree-lined streets and limited commercial development.
The City of Bloomfield Hills has been incorporated since 1932, and before that the area consisted mostly of farms and fruit orchards.
Detroit business leaders bought large plots in Bloomfield Hills for summer and weekend homes, and large homes eventually came to line Woodward Avenue and the city's other main roads.
Industrialists, including figures from the automotive industry, built extensive estates in Bloomfield Hills on a landscape of rolling hills and dense woodlands.
The City of Bloomfield Hills strongly regulates tree removal to preserve its woodland character, and a permit is required to remove any regulated tree.
Bloomfield Hills is home to the Cranbrook Educational Community, a National Historic Landmark.

Cranbrook was developed in the 1920s by newspaper magnate George Gough Booth, with a campus designed largely by architect Eliel Saarinen, and its schools, art museum and science institute remain one of the city's defining features.

hub.intro: Large homes, deep lots and wooded grounds make Bloomfield Hills a place where holiday lighting has to be planned, not improvised. Holiday Light Service brings more than two decades of holiday lighting experience, and your free estimate starts with a walk of the property.
hub.local_context: Bloomfield Hills grew from farms and fruit orchards into a city of estates after Detroit business leaders bought large plots for summer and weekend homes. Incorporated in 1932, it is still primarily residential, with tree-lined streets, rolling hills and dense woodlands, and the city requires a permit to remove regulated trees to protect that woodland character. The Cranbrook Educational Community, a National Historic Landmark, is part of its identity. For holiday lighting, that adds up to big rooflines, big trees and houses often seen from a distance, so every display is designed with scale and reach in mind.
highlights: Canopy and trunk lighting for the big trees on wooded estate grounds
Roofline designs scaled to large homes and long frontages
Permanent roofline outlines for wings, gables and garages

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Bloomfield Hills, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation for Bloomfield Hills, MI estates. Tree wraps, rooflines and entry lighting designed, installed and removed. Free estimate.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Bloomfield Hills, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Rooflines, tall trees and front entries lit at estate scale, with bucket-truck crews for the high work and takedown after the holidays.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Bloomfield Hills is a city of estates on rolling, wooded land, and the lighting has to match that scale. A long roofline with several gables, tall trees near the house and a front entry that anchors the facade are separate parts of one design, and each has to read from the road. The city regulates tree removal to protect its woodland character, so the trees on a lot are usually there for the long run. We make them the backbone of the display, with trunk wraps and canopy lighting set from the bucket where the grounds give it room. Rooflines get clean, even runs, and after the holidays we come back for all of it.
considerations: Design for the view from the road

On a large lot the house may sit well back from the street, so the display has to read at a distance. We think about sight lines from the road and the drive, then decide where brightness should build: the roofline, the entry or a stand of trees.

Mature hardwoods and evergreens can climb well past ladder height. We note tree heights, ground conditions and slope during the estimate, since rolling terrain affects where a bucket truck can set up safely and how close it can get.

A display at this scale draws on more outlets and longer runs than a typical house. The estimate maps the exterior power around the home and grounds, then balances the layout across circuits to help avoid tripped outlets on cold December evenings.
faq: Do you serve Bloomfield Township as well as the city?

The City of Bloomfield Hills is surrounded on most sides by Bloomfield Township, a separate municipality. The township sits between communities we already serve, so include your street address with the estimate request and we will confirm whether it falls within our service area.
How far ahead should a large property book?

The earlier the better. Larger displays take longer to design and install, and the install window commonly opens in October and closes in early December. Reaching out in August or September gives you the widest choice of dates, though later requests are still welcome.
Do you coordinate with our landscaper or property staff?

Gladly. On larger properties we plan around a landscaper, a caretaker or a property manager. Tell us who handles gate access and who approves the design, and we will keep that person informed from the estimate through takedown.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Bloomfield Hills, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Bloomfield Hills, MI commercial holiday lighting for offices, association entrances and managed estates, with restrained designs and a free estimate.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Bloomfield Hills, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Holiday lighting for offices, association entrances and managed estates, planned with owners and managers from walkthrough to removal.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Bloomfield Hills is primarily residential, with limited commercial development, so commercial holiday lighting here tends to mean something specific. It can be an office or professional building that wants a polished entrance for clients. It can be an association with a shared entrance to light, or a property manager handling the display for an owner who would rather not manage the details. Each of those projects needs one plan, a clear estimate and a crew that arrives prepared. We plan each display for its setting, install with bucket trucks for tall trees and building fronts, answer service calls during the season and take everything down after the holidays.
considerations: In a residential city, commercial lighting should look deliberate and understated. Warm white outlines, wrapped entry trees and a lit sign usually sit more comfortably here than a busy color mix. We design to the setting and show you the plan before anything goes up.

Association entrances and front drives often sit on grades, berms or planted beds. We look at footing for ladders and the bucket truck, the location of outlets near the sign, and how the display reads for drivers approaching from each direction.

If a property is gated or has staff on site, we confirm contacts, codes and access windows ahead of every visit. Crews stay within the areas in the plan, and one point of contact keeps the owner or manager informed all season.
faq: Do you light offices and association entrances in Bloomfield Hills?

Yes, along with estates run by a property manager. Any of them can start with a site walkthrough and a free estimate, and the work runs from design and installation with bucket-truck crews through in-season service and removal once the season wraps up.
Can a property manager handle the whole process?

Absolutely. A manager can schedule the walkthrough, review the estimate and coordinate access without the owner on site. We send a written plan for approval, keep one contact through the season and handle service calls and removal the same way.

Removal is part of every commercial estimate, alongside design, installation and in-season service. Nothing is left for staff to pull down after the holidays, and the written estimate spells out exactly what the season includes for your property.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Roofline Lighting in Bloomfield Hills, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Bloomfield Hills, MI permanent lighting: one continuous roofline outline across every wing of a large home, set from an app. Free estimate.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Bloomfield Hills, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: Roofline lighting built into the eaves of a large home, ready for December, game nights and quiet evenings, and run from an app.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: A seasonal display on a large Bloomfield Hills home is real work each fall and again after the holidays. Permanent lighting is installed once. A discreet track follows the roofline under the eaves, across wings, gables and garages, and stays quiet in daylight. At night, the app sets the colors, scenes and schedule: warm white through December, red and green for a holiday party, a quiet glow on weeknights. On a wooded lot, that outline also gives the house presence through the trees in every season. We design the runs around your architecture and set up the app with you.
considerations: Large homes often combine wings, dormers and rooflines at different heights. We plan corners, transitions and power feeds so the lighting reads as one continuous outline at night rather than a set of disconnected runs, even across a long frontage.

Permanent lighting mounts to the home, so check with the City of Bloomfield Hills about any review that applies to your property before installation. Bring the written estimate to that conversation; it shows where the track would run and how it attaches.
A welcome at the end of the drive

Among mature trees, a lit roofline marks the house for guests after dark and gives the property a warm look through bare winter branches. Set a nightly schedule in the app once, and the house lights itself at dusk from then on.
faq: Does permanent lighting work on a large Bloomfield Hills home?

It does. On a large house, plan on a longer first visit, since we walk every wing, gable and garage roofline and check the power before preparing the layout and the free estimate. Homes in nearby Oakland County communities can start the same way.
How visible is the track in daylight?

It mounts beneath the eaves and sits low, so from the street it is hard to pick out. On a home with distinctive trim or stonework, we walk through exactly where it will run and how it will look before anything is installed.
Should I choose permanent or seasonal lighting?

If you want lights mostly in December and like a fresh design each year, seasonal installation fits. If you would use the roofline for other holidays, family events or everyday accent light, permanent makes more sense on a home this size. We can talk through both at the estimate.
